grammar_focus: 两种现在时:一般现在时(习惯、反复、客观事实/规律) vs 现在进行时(此刻正在发生、这一阵临时在做),以及 always + 现在进行时(老是……,带抱怨/情绪)与一批 in 固定短语(in surprise / in a hurry / in the end / in trouble / in bed / in the dark)(原创承载 NCE3 L2 考点·美国小镇的老钟半夜敲十三下)
scene: 在我们镇上,市政厅上那座老钟老是惹麻烦。它日夜报时,大家都熟悉它那沉沉的钟声,镇上一直想筹钱把它修好,可钱总不够。奇怪的是:凌晨一点,这钟会敲十三下——其实就是一点,所以对这钟来说,十三等于一。多数夜里我躺在床上,惊讶地数着钟响。这一阵有件新鲜事:每晚钟楼里都有一点小灯在移动,有人半夜在上面忙活。今晚我终于抓起手电,穿过空荡荡的广场。借着手电光,我认出是照看隔壁小教堂、常给牧师帮忙的老戴尔先生。“这么晚你在上面干嘛?”我问。“我在修这口钟,”他轻声说,“这一阵我几乎每晚都上来。我不忍心看着全镇为一口老钟犯难。”戴尔先生年纪不小了,老是在鼓捣点什么,却从不放弃。到现在,钟还是敲十三下——可全镇学会了一笑,把它当成一点。

grammar_card.title: 两种现在时:一般现在时 & 现在进行时
grammar_card.intro: ①一般现在时——讲习惯、反复发生的事、客观事实/规律(The clock strikes the hours. / Water boils at 100°.);②现在进行时(am/is/are + doing)——讲此刻正在发生、或这一阵临时在做的事(A light is moving now. / These days it is happening.)。特别注意:always/constantly + 现在进行时,表示“老是……”,往往带点抱怨或情绪(That clock is always causing trouble!)。再记一批要整体背的 in 短语:in surprise(惊讶地)、in a hurry(匆忙)、in the end(最后)、in trouble(有麻烦)、in bed(在床上)、in the dark(在黑暗中)。

rows: 习惯、反复、客观事实/规律
The clock strikes the hours. / Water boils at 100°.
此刻正在发生 / 这一阵临时在做
A light is moving now. / These days it is happening.
That clock is always causing trouble!
一批要整体记的介词短语
in surprise / in a hurry / in the end / in trouble

specialRules.rule: 看到 now, right now, at the moment, these days, Listen!, Look! 多用现在进行时;看到 every day, usually, often, always(讲习惯) 多用一般现在时。
always + 现在进行时 不是单纯讲习惯,而是“老是……”,带抱怨或情绪色彩(He is always losing his keys! 他老是丢钥匙!)。
手电筒美语常说 flashlight(英式 torch);torchlight 指“手电筒的光”。本课已按美语写。

prelisten.q: Listen and answer — How many times does the clock strike at one o'clock?
options: It does not strike at all

passage: In our town, the old clock on the town hall is always causing trouble. It stands high above Main Street and strikes the hours day and night. Everyone knows its slow, heavy sound, and the town keeps trying to raise money to fix it. The strange thing is this: at one o'clock the clock strikes thirteen times. It is really one o'clock, but for our clock, thirteen equals one. Most nights I lie in bed and count the strokes in surprise. These days something new is happening. Every night a small light is moving inside the tower, and someone is working up there in the dark. Tonight I finally grab a flashlight and cross the empty square. By the torchlight I recognize old Mr. Dale, who looks after the little church next door and often helps the vicar there. 'What are you doing up here so late?' I ask. 'I am trying to fix the bell,' he says quietly. 'I come up here almost every night now. I hate to see the whole town in trouble over one old clock.' Mr. Dale is not a young man, and he is always working on something, but he never gives up. So far the clock still strikes thirteen, and the town just smiles and calls it one.
